# Traefik router reference

What `wikijs-<slug>.yml` looks like, why each section is there, and how Traefik picks it up.

## File location

```
<TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_CONFIG_DIR>\wikijs-<slug>.yml
```

On DOCKERHOST1: `C:\projects\traefik\dynamic\wikijs-<slug>.yml`.

The Traefik container mounts `C:\projects\traefik\dynamic` read-only as `/etc/traefik/dynamic`, with `--providers.file.watch=true` so changes are picked up automatically (typically within 2 seconds).

## Generated content

```yaml
# Generated by system-docs-domain skill — do not edit by hand.
# Created for system: docpilot
# Hostname:           docs.docpilot.se
# Redirect target:    /sv/docpilot/anvandardokumentation/?lang=sv

http:
  routers:
    wikijs-docpilot:
      rule: "Host(`docs.docpilot.se`)"
      entryPoints:
        - web
      service: wikijs-docpilot
      middlewares:
        - wikijs-forwarded-headers@file
        - wikijs-docpilot-redirect

  middlewares:
    wikijs-docpilot-redirect:
      redirectRegex:
        regex: "^https?://docs\\.docpilot\\.se/?$"
        replacement: "https://docs.docpilot.se/sv/docpilot/anvandardokumentation/?lang=sv"
        permanent: false

  services:
    wikijs-docpilot:
      loadBalancer:
        passHostHeader: true
        servers:
          - url: "http://wikijs-app:3000"
```

## Why each section

### Router

`Host(\`docs.docpilot.se\`)` matches only this exact hostname. Other systems on other hostnames get their own routers in their own files — no collisions.

`entryPoints: [web]` matches Traefik's port 80 entrypoint, which is what the Cloudflare Tunnel forwards to.

### Middlewares — order matters

Two middlewares applied in order:

1. **`wikijs-forwarded-headers@file`** — sets `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`. Lives in the **shared file** `wikijs-shared.yml` (created once for the whole platform; see `references/shared-middleware.md`). The `@file` suffix means "look in the file provider", not in Docker labels.

2. **`wikijs-<slug>-redirect`** — system-specific. Defined inline in this file because the redirect target is unique per system.

The shared middleware MUST run first so `X-Forwarded-Proto` is set before the redirect happens. If you swap the order, the redirect happens on `http://` URLs and breaks.

### Redirect regex

```yaml
regex: "^https?://docs\\.docpilot\\.se/?$"
replacement: "https://docs.docpilot.se/sv/docpilot/anvandardokumentation/?lang=sv"
permanent: false
```

Matches **only** the bare hostname (`/` or empty path). Anything deeper (`/sv/...`, `/login`, `/u/asset.png`) is NOT matched — it passes through to Wiki.js unchanged.

`permanent: false` → 302, not 301. This is intentional: if you change `redirect_target` later, browsers don't have a cached permanent redirect to the old target.

The dots in the hostname are escaped (`\\.`). Without escaping, `docs.docpilot.se` would also match `docsXdocpilotXse`, which isn't an issue in practice but is incorrect regex.

### Service

`http://wikijs-app:3000` is Docker DNS — resolves to the Wiki.js container on the `proxy` network. Both Traefik and Wiki.js must be on that network.

`passHostHeader: true` keeps the original `Host: docs.docpilot.se` when forwarding. Wiki.js needs this so it knows which host to use in absolute URLs.

## File watcher behaviour

Traefik watches the directory, not individual files. Adding/changing/deleting any file in `dynamic/` triggers a reload.

To verify a new file was loaded:

```powershell
docker logs traefik-gateway --tail 20 | Select-String "wikijs-docpilot"
```

Look for lines like `Provider event received {"providerName":"file","action":"created"...}`.

If a file has a YAML syntax error, Traefik logs it and skips that file but keeps the other routers running. Always `--dry-run` first if uncertain.

## Multiple systems

Each system gets its own file. With three systems:

```
dynamic/
├── wikijs.yml                 # legacy, prohat etc.
├── wikijs-shared.yml          # shared middleware (X-Forwarded-Proto)
├── wikijs-docpilot.yml        # docs.docpilot.se
├── wikijs-clippilot.yml       # docs.clippilot.se
└── wikijs-styrgruppskort.yml  # docs.styrgruppskort.se
```

Routers don't conflict because each matches a unique `Host(...)`. Service and middleware names are scoped per file (Traefik treats `wikijs-docpilot` in one file as different from `wikijs-clippilot` in another).

## Removal

Delete the file. Traefik picks up the deletion within ~2s. The route stops working immediately. The Cloudflare side (DNS + tunnel) must also be removed in the same operation, or users hit a 404 on Cloudflare's edge or a 502 from Traefik.

`configure_domain.py remove` does all three in the right order: DNS → tunnel → Traefik file.

## Common issues

**File written but `Host: ...` curl returns 404 from Traefik** — file watcher not active, or YAML syntax error. Check `docker logs traefik-gateway --tail 40` for parse errors.

**`Host: ...` returns 502 Bad Gateway** — Traefik can't reach `wikijs-app:3000`. Verify with `docker network inspect proxy` that `wikijs-app` is on the network. If not: `docker network connect proxy wikijs-app`.

**Redirect goes to `http://...` instead of `https://...`** — `wikijs-forwarded-headers` middleware not applied first. Check the file's `middlewares` order.

**Redirect happens on every page, not just `/`** — regex too greedy. The `?$` anchor at the end is critical.
